_: The vocabulary. One entry per hack, and every number on screen is in here
with the study it came from. A hack with no `source` does not ship - the
brand is a health app, and a number nobody can chase is worth less than no
icon    a lucide name in icon-sources/package/icons/<name>.svg
clock   where it sits in the day. Drives the day bar and the row order
chips   what it costs the viewer. One is the shipped default: one chip
read at arm's length beats two chips read by nobody
metric  the caption under the dial - what changes
value   what the dial counts up to. Text, so '+250%' and '-2 H' both work
dir     up | down | time. The dial's colour, and nothing else
source  the citation. Prose, because it is read by a person, not parsed

morning light.source: Sharkey/Eastman, Sleep Med 2014-15: morning bright light on waking advanced sleep/wake timing and circadian phase markers by about 2 h. Also Leproult, JCEM 2001: dim->bright (150->4500 lux) in the early morning raises plasma cortisol within 15 min, which is the same clock being set.

cold finish.source: Sramek et al., Eur J Appl Physiol 2000: immersion at 14 C raised plasma dopamine to 250% of baseline, rising gradually and staying up for hours with no crash after it. The 2 min chip is the shower-tail dose Huberman's synthesis settles on (1-3 min at 4-7 C), not the study's own hour.

walk after lunch.source: Sci Rep 2025 (s41598-025-07312-y): a 10 min walk taken immediately after glucose intake cut the peak from 181.9 to 164.3 mg/dL, p=0.028, d=0.73. That is -9.7%, rounded down. Self-selected pace, 3.8 km/h - a stroll, not a session.

last coffee.source: Caffeine's plasma half-life in healthy adults is about 5 h. Ten hours between the last cup and lights-out is two half-lives, so a quarter of the dose is left instead of the whole of it - 75% less than the same coffee taken at bedtime. Pure pharmacokinetics, no single trial: the number is arithmetic on a constant.

lights down.source: Phillips et al., PNAS 2019: evening room light suppresses melatonin, and the sensitivity spread is enormous - half the people tested lost 50% of their melatonin under less than 30 lux, which is dimmer than most living rooms. The dial states the benefit of dimming, which is the suppression not taken; the study measured the loss.

veg first.source: Shukla et al., Diabetes Care 2015;38:e98: the same meal eaten vegetables-and-protein-first rather than carbohydrate-first cut mean post-meal glucose by 28.6% at 30 min, 36.7% at 60 and 16.8% at 120, and the incremental AUC by 73%. Shukla 2019 (Diab Obes Metab) repeated it in prediabetes. -29% is the 30 min figure, the one a person would feel. The only entry in the table that costs nothing at all - it is an order, not a dose, which is why its chip reads 0 MIN.

7000 steps.source: Ding et al., Lancet Public Health 2025 (57 studies, 2014-2025, dose-response meta-analysis): 7000 steps a day against 2000 was associated with 47% lower all-cause mortality and 47% lower cardiovascular mortality. Observational, so association not cause, and the comparator matters - it is against 2000 steps, not against a person who already walks.

nose breathing.source: Balban et al., Cell Rep Med 2023 (Stanford): 5 min a day of cyclic sighing - long exhales - beat mindfulness meditation on both mood (p<0.05) and resting respiratory rate (p<0.05) over a month, and the people whose breathing slowed most were the ones whose mood rose most.

hydrate first.source: Ganio et al., Br J Nutr 2011 and Armstrong et al., J Nutr 2012: mild dehydration around 1-2% of body mass degrades vigilance, working memory and mood in both men and women. The +14% is the vigilance-error recovery reported in Ganio; treat it as directional, and prefer the plain claim - the deficit shows up long before thirst does.

stand up.source: Dunstan et al., Diabetes Care 2012: breaking 5 h of sitting with 2 min of light walking every 20 min cut the postprandial glucose incremental AUC by 24.1% against uninterrupted sitting. Restated here at the dose people will actually do - a few minutes an hour - so read it as the effect's size, not its exact schedule.

no screens.source: Chang et al., PNAS 2015: reading on a light-emitting device before bed pushed melatonin onset later, cut evening sleepiness and lengthened the time taken to fall asleep by about 10 min against a printed book, over five nights.

last meal early.source: Gu et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2020: the same meal eaten at 22:00 rather than 18:00 left overnight glucose higher and fat oxidation lower in the same people. The magnitude is the study's own peak-glucose difference; the 3 h chip is the founder's own rule in CORE_STORY.md - last meal two or three hours before bed.

fibre first.source: Reynolds et al., Lancet 2019 (185 prospective studies, 58 trials, 135 million person-years): 25-29 g of dietary fibre a day against under 15 g was associated with 15-30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, and the dose-response curve was still falling at 35 g. -20% is the middle of that band. Observational for the mortality end, though the trials support the mechanism.

lift twice.source: Momma et al., Br J Sports Med 2022 (meta-analysis of 16 cohort studies): 30-60 min a week of muscle-strengthening activity was associated with 10-17% lower risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular disease, total cancer and diabetes. The curve is J-shaped and flat past an hour - more is not better here, which is the unusual part and the reason the chip says 40 min a WEEK. Independent of aerobic activity; combined, the two are additive.

see people.source: Holt-Lunstad et al., PLoS Medicine 2010 (meta-analysis, 148 studies, 308 849 people, average 7.5 y follow-up): people with stronger social relationships had a 50% greater likelihood of survival, OR 1.50. The effect held across age, sex, health status and cause of death, and is comparable in size to quitting smoking. The only entry in this table whose dose is not a number, because the studies measure integration rather than minutes.

heat then cold.source: Laukkanen et al., JAMA Intern Med 2015 (Kuopio, 2315 men, 20 y): 2-3 sauna sessions a week associated with 27% lower cardiovascular mortality against once a week, and 4-7 a week with 50%. Observational, so association not cause - and the only entry here that is not free, which is why it is not in the shipped five.

sleep window.source: Placeholder - has no defensible number and must not ship until it does. Kept as the shape of an entry, not as content.
